name: Assisted Pull-Up Machine
summary: A machine with a counterweight that takes part of your body weight so you can practice the pull-up pattern with full range. Useful for building toward unassisted pull-ups.
setup: Set the assistance weight so you can finish your reps with good form; more weight means more help.
Step onto the platform or kneel on the pad and grab the handles.
Let the arms straighten and set the shoulder blades down before the first rep.
execution: Pull the elbows down toward your ribs.
Raise until your chin passes the handles while the chest stays up.
Lower slowly until the arms are fully straight, then repeat.
mistakes: Bouncing off the bottom: control the descent and keep tension in the shoulders.
Choosing too much assistance forever: reduce the assistance gradually as reps become easy.
Pulling mostly with the arms: lead with the shoulder blades and elbows.
Leaning back and turning it into a row: keep the torso mostly upright.
